title: Relation after initialization
statement: Let $W$ be a natural number and let a compiler size configuration have frame width $F$, dispatch position $D$, and space limit $S$. Suppose $3\le F$ and $8\le D$. Let $\mu$ assign an integer to each natural-number address, and let $i,j\in\mathbb Z$. If the initial machine memory at every address $a<S$ is the $W$-bit encoding of $\mu(a)$, and the two argument registers contain the $W$-bit encodings of $i$ and $j$, respectively, then after the initialization program is run, the machine is related at stack index $4$ to the light state with memory $\mu$ and local-variable values $0,i,j$ at indices $0,1,2$, and zero at every other index. Here the compiler size configuration includes the requirement that its word size fits its stated limits, pool, and stack.
hypotheses_covered: A natural-number word size and a compiler size configuration with frame width, dispatch position, limits, and stack count
The frame width is at least 3
The dispatch position is at least 8
A function from natural-number addresses to integers
Initial memory agrees with the W-bit encoding of μ(a) at every address below the space limit
The first argument register contains the W-bit encoding of i
The second argument register contains the W-bit encoding of j
